summary: Lemon-mustard vinaigrette is 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon Dijon, 1/4 teaspoon sea salt and 4 tablespoons olive oil shaken in a jar for 30 seconds, a 2:1 oil-to-acid ratio that makes 6 tablespoons.
glance: 6 tablespoons, enough for a great big bowl of greens
5 minutes prep; about 30 seconds to shake
about 2 parts oil to 1 part lemon juice
faq: What is the ratio for vinaigrette?
The traditional ratio is 3 parts oil to 1 part vinegar. With lemon juice the author prefers about 2:1, as in this recipe, but you should taste and adjust to your preferences and the salad.
How do you make vinaigrette without a blender or whisk?

The mustard is an emulsifier that keeps the oil suspended, so you can combine everything in a jar with a tight-fitting lid and shake vigorously for 30 seconds, with no need to drizzle in the oil while whisking.
Why add so much mustard to vinaigrette?
It tastes good, and it acts as an emulsifier, keeping the oil suspended in the acid.
How much salt does salad dressing need?
A lot. The salad is only lightly dressed, so if the straight dressing doesn't taste pretty strong, the salad will be underseasoned.
What can I add to this vinaigrette?
Finely minced fresh or dried herbs, garlic, shallots, citrus zest or spices. Meyer lemons give an even better flavor than standard Eurekas.
Why does dressing slide off my salad?
Wet leaves. Dry the greens thoroughly (the author likes a crank-style salad spinner) and dress them at the very last moment; delicate greens wilt within a few minutes of meeting the vinaigrette.

summary: Kinoko gohan is Japanese mushroom rice: mixed fresh mushrooms and a few dried shiitake are simmered 5 minutes in shoyu, sake, mirin and kombu, then that liquid cooks the rice, either in a rice cooker or in a covered pot for about 20 minutes.
glance: 2 cups Japanese-style rice, pre-soaked an hour if time permits
mushrooms 5 minutes; rice about 20 minutes in a pot, or a normal rice cooker cycle
Vegetarian, vegan and kosher; potentially gluten-free with tamari
faq: What mushrooms do you use for kinoko gohan?

A variety of fresh Asian mushrooms such as king oyster, oyster, maitake, shimeji, bunapi or shiitake, plus a few dried shiitake for umami. The author wouldn't use white button, crimini or portabella. A grocery store sampler pack is an easy way to get variety.
Can I make kinoko gohan in a rice cooker?
Yes, you can make the whole dish in the rice cooker: simmer the mushrooms in the liquid, strain, then add the rice and the measured liquid and cook on a normal cycle.
How is this different from traditional kinoko gohan?

The most traditional way is to make a separate dashi, use it to cook the mushrooms, and then use the mushroom cooking liquid for the rice. This recipe takes a shortcut and makes a light dashi at the same time as cooking the mushrooms.
How much liquid do I use for the rice?
Measure the strained mushroom liquid and add water to make 2 1/2 cups total for 2 cups of rice.
Is kinoko gohan vegan and gluten-free?
It is vegetarian, vegan and kosher, and potentially gluten-free if you use a gluten-free tamari in place of shoyu.
Do I need to rest the rice after cooking?
If possible, let it stand 10 minutes with the heat off, then fold in the mushrooms, toasted sesame oil and salt to taste. Serve hot or warm.

summary: Saffron-date posset sets cream with citric acid instead of eggs or starch: cream, date sugar and saffron are heated to 85°C, mixed with 7 grams of citric acid and chilled at least 2 hours, then garnished Persian-style.
glance: Prep 15 min, cook 45 min, total 1 hr, plus at least 2 hours chilling
cream, sugar (15% of the cream weight), citric acid (0.7%), heated to 85°C
sous vide at 85°C for 45 minutes, or on the stovetop
faq: What is posset?
A classic English dessert of cream set into a pudding with acid instead of starch or egg. It tastes only of cream, whatever you flavor it with, and the tartness of the citric acid.
What is the base ratio for posset?
Bring cream, sugar (15% of the cream weight) and any flavorings up to 85°C, stir in citric acid (0.7% of the cream weight), pour into ramekins and chill for two hours.
Why use citric acid instead of wine or ale?
Posset was traditionally set with wine or ale, but citric acid is much easier and more predictable.
Do I need sous vide to make posset?
No. This version infuses the saffron sous vide at 85°C for 45 minutes, but on the stovetop you infuse on low heat for 10 minutes, then raise the heat to medium and cook to 85°C.
What flavors work in posset?
Any flavor that can handle a little sour bite: honey, vanilla, jasmine, or here date sugar and saffron with fresh dates, candied preserved lemon peel, pistachios, pistachio oil and lemon thyme.
How long does posset take to set?
At least 2 hours, covered with plastic wrap in the refrigerator.

summary: An umami-packed vegan broth built from browned onion, carrot and celery, tomato paste, Marmite, star anise, dried shiitake and kombu, cooked 20 minutes at high pressure in a pressure cooker; yields about 1 liter.
glance: browning about 15 minutes, then 20 minutes at high pressure
Vegetarian and vegan; gluten-free depending on your opinion of Marmite
faq: What is a good vegetable stock not?
A pot of leftover onion skins, half-moldy carrot trimmings and other dross boiled until it dies a second death. That gives a watery, bitter, insipid, poorly balanced liquid.
Which vegetarian ingredients are high in umami?
Tomatoes, dried shiitake mushrooms, Marmite, kombu and parmesan. This broth includes the first four and omits the parmesan to stay vegan, balanced so no single one dominates.
Why add star anise to broth?
Research mentioned in Heston Blumenthal's The Fat Duck Cookbook shows compounds in star anise, cooked with sulfur from onions and other alliums, release new flavor chemicals that enhance umami.
What is the difference between stock and broth?

A stock is a base ingredient, left relatively unseasoned so you can reduce it. A broth is a plain but fully seasoned soup you can eat as is. This recipe is a broth, but works as a stock if you cut the salt to 5 grams, and you can then reduce it by 50%.
How do I make the broth crystal clear?
Use Dave Arnold's agar clarification, the way to go for a consomme or ravioli en brodo.
What can I use the broth for?
As the basis of a rustic soup (the author suggests French onion), to cook grains in, or to add background complexity to a sauce.

summary: Turkish chickpea and potato stew with baharat: onion, garlic and tomato paste are browned, 2 tablespoons of baharat bloomed for 10 seconds, then crushed tomatoes and potatoes simmer 10 minutes before chickpeas simmer at least 10 more.
glance: about 10 minutes for the potatoes, then at least 10 more with the chickpeas
2 tablespoons Turkish baharat plus 1/2 teaspoon cayenne
Persian rice pilaf, plain basmati or couscous
Gluten-free; vegan with olive oil instead of butter

summary: Chile con limon (chile para fruta) is a tangy, spicy, salty Mexican seasoning for fruit and vegetables; this homemade smoked version mixes smoked paprika, salt and citric acid, and can be stirred into olive oil as a sauce.
glance: 4 teaspoons of powder or 2 tablespoons of sauce
smoked paprika, salt, citric acid, optional olive oil
yield: 4 teaspoons of powder or 2 tablespoons of sauce
faq: What is chile con limon?

A chile powder that is tangy, spicy and a little salty, also called chile para fruta. It is eaten on fruit like mango and watermelon, and on vegetables, peanuts and popcorn, or used as a table seasoning.
Where can I buy chile con limon?
At any Mexican grocery, under names like Znax Chilito En Polvo, Pico Sitos or Pica Limon.
Why does it contain citric acid?

Citric acid gives a citrusy, acidic flavor (leaning towards lime) without the taste of a particular fruit or any added water. It is present in large quantities in citrus fruits. You can find it on Amazon or in bulk at better grocery stores.
What chiles can I use?

Spanish smoked paprika is a non-traditional choice used here. You can also use ancho, pasilla, morita or any other Mexican chile. For best results use whole dried chiles: remove the seeds and stems, toast lightly in a pan, cool and grind.
How do I turn it into a sauce?
Stir the powder into extra-virgin olive oil, as in the photo, and use it as a dipping sauce.

summary: A piquant red chili sauce for tamales: ancho, morita and aji amarillo chiles soaked 15 minutes in boiling water, blended with browned onion, garlic, fire-roasted tomatoes, oregano and cocoa; enough for at least 20-30 tamales.
glance: 4 ancho, 2 morita (or 1 chipotle in adobo), 1 dried aji amarillo
faq: What chiles go in red chili sauce for tamales?
Four ancho, two morita (or one chipotle in adobo) and one dried aji amarillo, with the seeds and stems removed.
How do you make the sauce?

Soak the torn chiles in 4 cups of boiling water for 15 minutes in a blender jar. Brown the onion and unpeeled garlic in a skillet, peel the garlic, then add everything to the blender with the vegetable base, fire-roasted tomatoes, oregano, cocoa powder and salt and blend on high for 1 minute.
How thick should the sauce be?
A thick sauce. If it is too thick, add a bit more water, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
What tamale fillings go with it?
The author likes a large dose of it moistening tamales filled with cubes of tofu and zucchini, or with black beans.
Can I reheat leftover tamales?
Yes. They reheat beautifully in the microwave, and leftovers make a good breakfast.

summary: Syrian red lentil soup (shurbat addes), adapted from Poopa Dweck's Aromas of Aleppo: red lentils simmered about 40 minutes until they puree, then finished with a fried garlic, coriander and salt paste.
glance: 8 cups: 8 appetizer servings or 4 main course servings
about 40 minutes, until the lentils dissolve into a puree
2 cups red lentils (don't substitute brown, green, black or French)
faq: What lentils do you use for Syrian red lentil soup?
Red lentils, available at natural or health food stores. Don't substitute brown, green, black or French lentils.
How long do you cook the lentils?
Rinse and pick them over, boil them in 2 quarts of water, then simmer about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally so they don't stick and scorch, until they have dissolved into a puree.
How do you season the soup?
Grind 6 cloves of garlic, the coriander seed and salt into a coarse paste, fry it in olive oil for about 1 minute without burning the garlic, and add it to the soup to simmer a bit longer.
What garnish goes on shurbat addes?

Fresh cilantro, ground cumin, Aleppo pepper, dukkah or chili flakes, with lemon wedges on the side. Aleppo pepper is specific to Syrian food and hard to find in US stores; dukkah, an Egyptian spice blend, is a great alternative.
How thick should the soup be?
The author prefers it moderately thin, as a light first course, but thick works as a main dish. Adjust the texture with water first, then salt.

summary: Quickie amba is a fast stand-in for Iraqi pickled mango condiment: diced slightly underripe mango tossed with minced preserved lemon and harissa, served at room temperature and kept refrigerated for a few days.
glance: 6 as a condiment at a meal
a few days in the refrigerator
Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and kosher (check the preserved lemon and harissa labels for gluten)
faq: What is amba?

A pickled mango condiment, served on sabich, an Iraqi-Jewish eggplant sandwich with fried eggplant, Israeli salad, hummus, tahina, hardboiled egg and cucumber pickle. It isn't easy to find in America.
What kind of mango for quickie amba?
Slightly underripe is better, but not rock hard. Dice it finely.
What do I serve quickie amba with?
Sabich, or any Middle Eastern meal: a rice and chickpea pilaf, chickpea cakes or a tagine.
How long does quickie amba keep?
A few days in the refrigerator. Serve it at room temperature.
Is it gluten-free?
It is vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and kosher, but check the ingredients of the preserved lemon and harissa if you need it gluten-free.

summary: A Caribbean-inspired bowl of basmati rice cooked with coconut milk, topped with black beans, pan-fried plantains, avocado, mango and a moderately spicy mango salsa; the whole meal comes together in about 20 minutes.
glance: about 20 minutes for a weeknight supper
fried about 3 minutes on one side, about 2 on the other
coconut rice reheats well in the microwave
faq: How do you make coconut rice?
Cook basmati rice in your usual way, on the stovetop or in a rice cooker, but replace one can's worth of water with a 13-ounce can of coconut milk and add an extra quarter cup of water.
Can I make the coconut rice ahead?
Yes. It reheats really well, so you can make it the day before and warm it in the microwave at dinner time.
How do you cook the plantains?

Pan fry coins about 1/4 inch thick in shimmering oil over medium-high heat, in a single layer, about 3 minutes until brown on one side, then about 2 more minutes on the other until browned and tender. Sprinkle with Kosher salt.
Is this a good dish for kids?
Yes. They can pick and choose the ingredients they enjoy, especially if you serve all the components separately and let diners assemble their own.
How spicy is the mango salsa?
Moderately spicy, from 1 to 2 jalapeno or serrano peppers. It also works on a wide variety of other meals, from Mexican to southeast Asian.
How is the dish served?
Divide the rice among four bowls and top with plantains, black beans, avocado, mango, cilantro and sauce, with lime quarters to squeeze over the top.
